Emergence Ladder

How Bayesian-like inference arises naturally from self-organisation across levels: physics → chemistry → evolution → brain → mind.

The universe doesn’t use our models; it exhibits regularities that we later describe with them. Across scales, systems that persist in noisy environments shape themselves so that their internal dynamics match external structure—this looks like inference: predicting and reducing surprising states. Evolution didn’t read Bayes; it selects for systems that persist. Persistence in a noisy world requires accurate expectations. Hence, structures that survive are those whose dynamics behave like inference machines — whether molecules, brains, or scientific communities.

Each rung adds feedback that stabilises structure against noise. Stability requires expectations that fit the world — which is why dynamics appear “Bayesian-like.”

Physics

  • Open systems form order by dissipating energy (Prigogine-type phenomena).
  • Variational & least-action principles describe stable trajectories.

Chemistry

  • Autocatalytic sets and lipid membranes create self-maintaining cycles.
  • States inside the membrane covary with outside conditions → proto “aboutness”.

Evolution

  • Selection filters lineages that best anticipate recurring contexts.
  • Genes as priors; environments as evidence; gene pool as posterior.

Brain

  • Predictive coding minimises prediction error via learning and action.
  • Attention = precision weighting on error signals.

Mind & Culture

  • Explicit models (math, science) mirror implicit stabilising dynamics.
  • Institutions extend inference across people and time (epistemic niche).
